rv.q: This affecting King Lear variation suggests she has a genuinely fresh perspective—warm and wise but also tough-minded and wickedly funny—to bring to depictions of the Asian-American experience in theater.
But when it doesn’t work (and I fear Laowang falls into this category), it’s a real letdown.
Lin is certainly a talented playwright, and Laowang is a wonderful introduction.
Laowang is an exuberant romp, with the added benefit of insights about human folly and other timeless subjects.

cn.t: Alex Lin's Chinatown riff on King Lear earns mostly positive reviews for its vigorous energy and comic surprises, though one critic finds it less illuminating than the source material it adapts.
